title: Domains and Ranges of Reciprocal Quotients
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = 2 and g(x) = x^2 + 1. Find the natural domains and ranges of f, g, the quotient f / g, and the quotient g / f.
finalAnswer: D_f = (-\infty, \infty),\ R_f = \{2\};\quad D_g = (-\infty, \infty),\ R_g = [1, \infty);\quad D_{f/g} = (-\infty, \infty),\ R_{f/g} = (0, 2];\quad D_{g/f} = (-\infty, \infty),\ R_{g/f} = \left[\frac{1}{2}, \infty\right)

steps.title: Find the Domains and Ranges of f and g
steps.explanation: The constant function f(x) = 2 is defined for all real x and outputs only 2. The quadratic function g(x) = x^2 + 1 is defined for all real x, and since x^2 >= 0, we have x^2 + 1 >= 1, giving range [1, infinity).
steps.why: Polynomials have domain (-infinity, infinity), and x^2 >= 0 bounds x^2 + 1 below by 1.

steps.title: Analyze the Domain and Range of f / g
steps.explanation: Since g(x) = x^2 + 1 >= 1 > 0 for all real x, the denominator never vanishes, so D_{f/g} = (-infinity, infinity). Because x^2 + 1 takes all values in [1, infinity), its reciprocal 1/(x^2 + 1) takes all values in (0, 1], and multiplying by 2 yields (0, 2].
steps.why: Taking the reciprocal of an interval [1, infinity) reverses the inequality to (0, 1], and scaling by 2 maps (0, 1] to (0, 2].

steps.title: Analyze the Domain and Range of g / f
steps.explanation: Since the constant denominator f(x) = 2 is never zero, D_{g/f} = (-infinity, infinity). Dividing each value in the range [1, infinity) of g by 2 gives the range [1/2, infinity).
steps.why: Scaling a function with range [1, infinity) by the positive constant 1/2 scales the range to [1/2, infinity).
